name: claim-card
description:
The name-claim offer — the page's whole conversion, stated once. An eyebrow, a heading, a lede, a two-column benefit list, a price block with the struck list price hung off it as a badge, and one full-width action. This is the SECOND life of this unit: the first had an inline field, a submit and a full-bleed offer strip, and the product removed all three — the field because the destination asks for the name anyway, the strip because the offer changed shape into the badge. The unit follows the product; a composite depicting a superseded design is drift wearing a docs page.

The badge is absolutely positioned off the paid price's right edge so it contributes no width: the amount you pay stays optically centred, which a struck price set inline beside it defeated. The saving under the strike is the claim itself — a struck number alone leaves the reader to do the subtraction.

base.$description: CONTAINER. This unit establishes an inline-size container named after itself, so anything inside it responds to the width of THIS BOX rather than the window. `inline-size: 100%` is the container's REQUIRED companion: `container-type: inline-size` makes the box's width independent of its contents, so a container with no width of its own collapses to zero. The border is `rule-mark` thick in the accent at quarter strength — the same edge the live card wore as a utility, now traceable.

eyebrow.$description: Composes `text--eyebrow`; only the colour is this unit's. `accent-ink` — the brand yellow darkened exactly far enough to be text — because this card IS the accent surface of the page: sunflower raw measures 1.75:1 on it, the ink 5.80:1.

benefits.$description: Two columns that become one below the fold-in width, via `auto-fit` rather than a breakpoint — the count varies and a fixed column rule drops the tail. `text-align: start` on purpose: a centred list of four items has four different left edges and reads as ragged.

benefit.$description: The bullet is an element in the accent, not a list marker — a marker cannot be coloured separately from its text in every engine, and colour is the only thing distinguishing it.

price.$description: A bordered block, not a bare tint — the tint alone let the price float in the panel with nothing marking where it started and ended.

figures.$description: The figures share a baseline row; the terms sit under them as their own row.

now.$description: The paid price, with the struck one hung off its RIGHT edge as a badge. The badge is absolutely positioned inside this wrapper so it adds no width and the amount stays optically centred — a strike set inline pushed the real number off centre, the one thing the offer must not do.

was.$description: Solid terracotta, not a tinted outline — a discount badge drawn as chrome was not doing its one job. Cream on `terracotta-strong` measures 5.70:1, so the strike survives being small AND being struck. Rotated off the grid the way a stamp is, which is what it is.

was-price.$description: The strike sits on the price alone — set on the badge it propagates into the saving line below it, striking the very number the badge exists to state.

off.$description: The saving, stated as a number, stacked under the struck price — the strike says what it WAS; alone it leaves the reader to do the subtraction. `accent-surface` measures 5.25:1 on this ground; the deeper yellows in the ramp read 4.03 and 3.34 and this line is small, so 4.5 rules.

terms.$description: Under the figures, quiet. It qualifies the number; it does not share its line.

action.$description: The one action on the card, sized to be it: the claim is the whole point of this block, so the button is the largest control on it rather than a link under a paragraph. The inner `btn` stretches to the part's full width.

dot.$description: The bullet, as an element rather than a list marker.

quiet.$description: Without the accent edge, for a surface where the card is one of several rather than the page's whole point.

a11y.note: A named `<section>`, so it is a landmark a screen reader can jump to — this is the page's conversion and it should be reachable without reading everything above it. The benefit list is a real `<ul>`, which is what announces 'list, four items'. The struck price and its saving are real text inside the landmark, not imagery: a reader hears the offer, not just the price.
